finding: Extensive omental caking, pelvic peritoneal implants, small-volume ascites, and bilateral adnexal masses. No thoracic metastasis.
impression: Advanced tubo-ovarian malignancy suspected, radiographic FIGO IIIC pattern with high peritoneal tumor burden.

finding: Marked decrease in omental and peritoneal disease after three cycles of neoadjuvant carboplatin/paclitaxel. Ascites nearly resolved.
impression: Partial radiographic response with substantially decreased peritoneal disease burden.

impression: New limited pelvic/peritoneal recurrent disease without liver or thoracic metastasis.

impression: New measurable low-volume peritoneal and pelvic nodal recurrent disease without bowel obstruction.

finding: Multiple enlarging but low-volume peritoneal implants, largest 2.6 cm, including a right paracolic implant abutting bowel serosa, several small ill-defined nodules along the sigmoid/small-bowel mesentery, and a left pelvic node 1.8 cm short axis. Small ascites. No definite thoracic, hepatic, osseous, or upper-abdominal critical-site metastasis.
impression: Interval progression with abdomen/pelvis-confined measurable peritoneal and pelvic nodal disease. Mesenteric nodularity, bowel-serosal abutment and small ascites create an intermediate resectability profile; CT alone does not prove R0 feasibility.

Small ascites. No definite root-of-superior-mesenteric-artery lesion, porta hepatis/hepatogastric-ligament mass, splenic-hilar lesion, lesser-sac lesion >1 cm, suprarenal retroperitoneal node, liver metastasis, thoracic metastasis, or osseous metastasis. Impression: Interval progression with abdomen/pelvis-confined measurable peritoneal and pelvic nodal disease; intermediate resectability profile; CT alone does not prove R0 feasibility.

finding: FDG-avid peritoneal implants SUVmax 10.1 and left pelvic nodal disease SUVmax 7.6. Uptake remains confined to abdomen/pelvis. No FDG-avid thoracic, hepatic, osseous, or suprarenal nodal metastases. No bowel obstruction.
impression: Metabolically active abdomen/pelvis-confined recurrence. Absence of occult distant FDG-avid disease keeps local strategy assessment reasonable, but PET/CT cannot clear small peritoneal, bowel-serosal, or mesenteric disease for complete cytoreduction.

Impression: Metabolically active abdomen/pelvis-confined recurrence; PET/CT alone cannot prove complete cytoreduction feasibility.

finding: Focused surgical-resectability addendum after CT/PET. DWI shows multifocal peritoneal implants, right paracolic bowel-serosal contact, sigmoid/small-bowel mesenteric nodularity, and mixed nodular plus plaque-like/infiltrative morphology. No dominant SMA-root mass >1 cm, lesser-sac lesion >1 cm, porta-hepatis/hepatogastric-ligament mass, splenic-hilar mass, suprarenal retroperitoneal node, or moderate/large ascites.
impression: Intermediate resectability profile on WB-DWI/MRI. Absence of dominant SMA-root or upper-abdominal critical-site masses is favorable, while plaque-like/infiltrative mesenteric and bowel-serosal disease lowers confidence in complete gross resection from imaging alone.
raw_text: WB-DWI/MRI resectability review: Multifocal peritoneal implants, right paracolic bowel-serosal contact, sigmoid/small-bowel mesenteric nodularity, and mixed nodular plus plaque-like/infiltrative morphology. No dominant SMA-root mass >1 cm, lesser-sac lesion >1 cm, porta-hepatis/hepatogastric-ligament mass, splenic-hilar mass, suprarenal retroperitoneal node, or moderate/large ascites. Impression: Intermediate resectability profile; infiltrative mesenteric and bowel-serosal disease lowers confidence in complete gross resection from imaging alone.
